---
title: Generalized decomposition R2
---

# Description

The GDR2 prior [@aguilarGeneralizedDecompositionPriors2024] is a global-local shrinkage prior that generalizes [R2D2](gen_linear_regression/r2d2.html) by replacing the Dirichlet decomposition of the total explained variance with other distributions on the simplex. From this perspective the R2D2 prior is a special case, and many alternative decompositions are possible. In particular, one useful alternative is the Logistic-Normal distribution, because it allows for a flexible way to encode prior dependence between the variance proportions.

# Definition

For a linear model:

$$
\begin{align}
y_i &\sim \text{normal}(\mu_i,\sigma^2) \\
\mu_i &= \alpha + \sum_{k=1}^{K}\beta_k x_{ik}
\end{align}
$$

The GDR2 prior is:

$$
\begin{align}
\beta_k &\sim \text{normal}\left(0,\sigma^2\phi_k\tau^2\right) \\
\tau^2 &= \frac{R^2}{1-R^2} \\
R^2 &\sim \text{beta}(\mu_{R^2},\varphi_{R^2}) \\
\phi &\sim p(\nu_\phi) \\
\sigma &\sim p(\sigma) \\
\alpha &\sim p(\alpha)
\end{align}
$$

where $\phi=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_K)$ lies on the simplex,

$$
\phi_k \geq 0,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^{K}\phi_k=1.
$$

The proportions $\phi_k$ determine how the global scale $\tau^2$ is allocated among the regression coefficients. The GDR2 framework allows different distributions for $\phi$; the Logistic-Normal distribution is the principal alternative to the Dirichlet distribution considered in the paper by @aguilarGeneralizedDecompositionPriors2024.

For a symmetric Logistic-Normal decomposition, let

$$
\eta \sim \text{normal}_K(\mu_\phi,\Sigma_\phi)
$$

and transform to the simplex using

$$
\phi_k =
\frac{\exp(\eta_k)}
{\sum_{j=1}^{K}\exp(\eta_j)}.
$$

The mean vector $\mu_\phi$ and covariance matrix $\Sigma_\phi$ determine the prior distribution and dependence structure between the variance proportions. Setting $\mu_{\phi,k}=0$ for all $k$ gives a symmetric prior for the variance proportions.

# Things to specify

Priors on $\alpha$ and $\sigma$.

Hyperparameters $\mu_{R^2}$ and $\varphi_{R^2}$ for the prior on $R^2$.

Hyperparameters $\mu_\phi$ and $\Sigma_\phi$ for the Logistic-Normal prior on the simplex.
